source_evidence: An index fund may not perfectly track its index. For example, a fund may only invest in a sampling of the securities in the market index, in which case the fund’s performance may be less likely to match the index. An index fund may underperform its index because of fees and expenses, trading costs, and tracking error.
answer: Tracking error is the gap between an index fund’s performance and the performance of the index it aims to track. For instance, a fund that holds only a sample of the index’s securities may be less likely to match the index. Underperformance means the fund returns less than its index; fees and expenses, trading costs, and tracking error can contribute to this.
